chunks: Muhammad narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibn Ribat, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ajlan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A woman performing Tamattu' arrives [at Mecca], and she sees blood. What should she do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'She performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf by the House. And if she does not become pure, when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water upon herself, enters into Ihram for Hajj, and goes out to Mina, and fulfills all the rituals. When she does that, then everything is permissible for her except the bed of her husband.'

He (the narrator) said: 'I and Ubaydullah ibn Salih heard this Hadith in the Mosque. So Ubaydullah went to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), and he came out to me and said: I have asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the narration of Ajlan, so he narrated to me with approximately what we heard from Ajlan.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills in Mecca)
key_terms.طَافَتْ بِالْبَيْتِ: She performed Tawaf around the Kaaba
key_terms.فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا: The marital bed (sexual intercourse with husband)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعَةٌ: A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a location near Mecca for Hajj rituals)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman performing Tamattu' Hajj who gets her period upon arrival in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific fiqh of Hajj al-Tamattu' for women whose menstruation or postpartum bleeding persists until the Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah). It establishes that such a woman delays her Tawaf al-Ifadah until she is pure, performing Sa'i and staying in Mina, with the key scholarly implication being that her Ihram is not broken but merely suspended, allowing her to complete the Hajj rites and resume marital relations with her husband upon final purification and completion.
